label: rem:dressed-particle-properties
title: Composition, stability, and Markov-trace functoriality of dressing
html:
Remark. Composition, stability, and Markov-trace functoriality of dressing

Composition. Dressing is not generally invertible. Stripping electrons changes the binding subword via the SDP. However, dressings compose:

  \mathrm{dress}_{S_2} \circ \mathrm{dress}_{S_1}
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{dress}_{S_1 \oplus S_2}

Here \oplus concatenates shell data when the combined Z remains SDP-feasible. Partial dressing (0 < Z' < Z_{\max}) yields ions.

Stability under dressing. The Frobenius-stability index of P_{\mathrm{dressed}} is monotonically non-decreasing along the dressing chain toward closed-shell noble-gas configurations (Z \in \{2, 10, 18, 36, 54, 86\}). Each shell closure is a \mu \ge 2 multi-operator fixed point of the SDP. Breaking the bond requires simultaneously breaking every tight dual block. Noble-gas objects are therefore local terminal objects of the dressing sub-diagram of \mathbf{Conf}.

Functoriality of the Markov trace. Under dressing, the Markov trace transforms as:

  \mathrm{tr}_M(P_{\mathrm{dressed}})
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}_M(P_{\mathrm{bare}}) \cdot
  \prod_{\lambda \in \mathcal{S}^*(S, q)} w_\lambda^{\,\langle \pi_\lambda, \Phi^* \rangle}

Here \mathcal{S}^*(S, q) is the SDP active support and w_\lambda are the block shadow prices. For \mu(S, q) = 1, this collapses to the scalar-LP product. For \mu \ge 2, the full matrix shadow contributes.
